faq.a: Abderrahim represents Arabic عبد الرحيم, meaning servant of al-Raḥīm (“the Most Merciful”).

faq.q: What is the origin of Abderrahim?
faq.a: The name is Arabic and is a compound of عبد and الرحيم.
Yes. The underlying compound is عبد الرحيم (ʿAbd al-Raḥīm).

faq.q: What is the root of Abderrahim?
faq.a: عبد is related to ع ب د; الرحيم is related to ر ح م, associated with mercy.
Abderrahim is a traditional Muslim personal name because it contains a compound invoking al-Raḥīm, a divine epithet in Islamic tradition.
This record does not establish Abderrahim as an explicitly named Qur'anic person; the compound's religious meaning is distinct from personal-name attestation in the text.

faq.q: What does Abderrahim mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, the name means servant of al-Raḥīm; the compound combines عبد with الرحيم.
The supplied “ab-der-ra-him” is an approximate pronunciation; local pronunciations vary.

faq.q: Is Abderrahim a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: The record classifies Abderrahim as masculine, consistent with traditional usage; regional frequency data is not supplied.
